data.content_ref: inline:The target states a substantive relation (inheritance + reduction) but its refutation condition is internally contradictory in a way that undermines the proposal's coherence. It claims 05b29af78bfb INHERITS from SRC_004 'the core thesis that the genuine-vs-compliance distinction is false for verifiable tasks,' yet simultaneously posits the relation is 'refuted if SRC_004's argument turns out to be about outcome-frequentism rather than internalist-vs-externalist epistemology.' But if the inherited core thesis is that 'the genuine-vs-compliance distinction is false for verifiable tasks' — a claim about verifiable task outcomes — then SRC_004's argument IS about outcome properties (frequentism/verification), not about internalist-vs-externalist epistemology. The target thus frames the very thing it says would refute the relation as if it were external to the inherited thesis, when it is actually constitutive of it. The proposal cannot coherently inherit an outcome-based thesis while making the relation contingent on the source NOT being outcome-based. This is not merely a missing scope item; it is a substantive incoherence in the stated relation between the endpoints.
